ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $ \triangle ABC$, $ \angle ACB = 90^\circ$, D is the midpoint of $ AB$, $ ED \perp AB$ intersects $ AC$ at point E, $ \tan \angle EBC = \frac{3}{4}$. What is the value of $ \tan \angle ABE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} In $\triangle EBC$, we have $\angle ECB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \tan\angle EBC=\frac{CE}{BC}=\frac{3}{4}$.\\
Let $CE=3k$, $BC=4k$, so $BE=5k$.\\
Since $D$ is the midpoint of $AB$ and $ED\perp AB$,\\
$\therefore AE=BE=5k$,\\
$\therefore \angle ABE=\angle BAE$, $AC=8k$,\\
In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \tan\angle CAB=\frac{BC}{AC}=\frac{4k}{8k}=\frac{1}{2}$.\\
$\therefore$ The tangent of $\angle ABE$ is $\boxed{\frac{1}{2}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is right triangle ABC, A is at the upper left, C is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, AC is vertical, CB is horizontal, E is located on AC, D is located on AB, and a line segment perpendicular to AB is drawn from E to D. Reasoning: Because E is on AC and ∠ACB=90°, ∠ECB=90°, so triangle EBC is a right triangle. It is known that tan∠EBC=CE/BC=3/4. Let CE=3k and BC=4k, then BE=5k. D is the midpoint of AB, and ED⊥AB, so ED is the perpendicular bisector of AB. Point E is on the perpendicular bisector, therefore AE=BE=5k. Thus triangle ABE is an isosceles triangle, ∠ABE=∠BAE. Also because E is on AC, ∠BAE=∠CAB. AC=AE+CE=5k+3k=8k. In right triangle ABC, tan∠CAB=BC/AC=4k/8k=1/2. Therefore tan∠ABE=tan∠CAB=1/2.
